primary_claim: Rephrasing the ambiguous Stages-Oversight benchmark questions into a pure classification task (Stages-Oversight-Rephrased) reveals that frontier LLMs (claude-3.5-sonnet, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini) significantly exceed random-chance accuracy at distinguishing evaluation from deployment prompts, and some models also show behavioral adaptation (Stages-Oversight-Procedural) even when they fail explicit classification, indicating LLMs are more situationally aware than the original Stages-Oversight benchmark suggested.

effect.metric: accuracy on Stages-Oversight-Rephrased vs. random chance (50%)
effect.value: frontier LLMs (claude-3.5-sonnet, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini) significantly exceed 50% chance (one-way binomial test, alpha=0.001, Bonferroni corrected); predecessor models do not surpass chance

contradicts_or_qualifies: the original Stages-Oversight benchmark (Laine et al.) found most LLMs score around or below random chance at distinguishing evaluation from deployment prompts; Stages-Oversight-Rephrased shows frontier LLMs significantly exceed chance, suggesting the earlier low scores were due to question ambiguity rather than a lack of capability
stated_future_work: test the ability of LLMs to categorize prompts that blur the lines between evaluation and deployment
test deployment scenarios more realistic or relevant to the threat scenario, such as multi-turn conversations and internal deployment where labs use LLMs/agents for AI R&D
test if LLMs can execute more complex/concerning/nuanced behavior shifts between evaluation and deployment, such as vulnerable code generation or tricking/coordinating with a monitoring LLM
limitations_stated: gpt-4o-mini often answered Stages-Oversight incorrectly because it seemingly misunderstood the yes-no question, not because it lacked situational awareness
instances of mismatch between performance on Stages-Oversight-Rephrased and Stages-Oversight-Procedural are difficult to explain
the unusually low performance of gpt-4, gpt-4o, and gpt-4o-mini on the procedural task may just be due to poor capability elicitation
did not test 'reasoning' LLMs such as OpenAI's o1 because their explicit chain-of-thought would create an unfair comparison
cannot assume the Stages-Oversight-Procedural baseline score is 50%; baseline scores varied widely within and between task variants
quote: These results suggest that frontier LLMs are far better at distinguishing evaluation and deployment prompts than previously thought.
